title: Kidney stone shock wave treatment (lithotripsy)
what: A stone in the kidney or ureter is broken up by shock waves from outside, through the skin. There are no cuts. The small pieces then pass out with your urine.
why: For small stones that do not pass on their own or cause pain.
duration: the procedure usually takes 30 to 60 minutes; you often go home the same day
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Pregnancy. The procedure is not done during pregnancy
If you have a fever now or your pain got worse

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood and urine tests, and an ultrasound or CT scan. Your clinic will give you the list. A urine infection is usually treated first.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for a few hours before, especially if you get pain relief through a vein or general anesthesia. Your clinic will give you the exact time.

prepare.title: Bowel
prepare.text: Sometimes you are advised to have a light dinner the day before, without foods that cause gas. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Getting home
prepare.text: Arrange for someone to drive you home.

bring: Your referral and scans of the stone
steps: You change into a gown, and often a cannula is put into a vein
You get pain relief or light sedation
You lie on the table, and the stone is found with X-ray or ultrasound
A soft cushion of the machine is pressed against your skin
The machine sends shock waves. You hear clicks
After the procedure, you rest while staff watch you
feel: The shock waves feel like clicks or taps on your skin
It may be unpleasant. Pain relief helps
Afterwards: a bruise or soreness where the waves were aimed
after: Drink more water, unless your doctor said otherwise
For a few days, your urine may be pink
The pieces pass with your urine over days or weeks. There may be pain, like colic
Sometimes you are asked to pee through a strainer, to give the stones for testing
In a few weeks, you have a check-up ultrasound or X-ray
red_flags: A fever over 38 degrees, or chills
Strong pain that does not ease with pain medicine
Bright blood with clots in your urine

faq.a: It is usually bearable. You get pain relief or light sedation. Later, it may hurt when the pieces pass.

faq.q: Can every stone be broken up from outside?
faq.a: No. Large and very hard stones are sometimes removed another way. A urologist decides based on your scan.

reminders.text: Kidney stone treatment tomorrow. Arrange for someone to take you home. Eat only until the time your clinic gave you.
